title: 第 47 課｜漢彌頓－雅可比方程：把力學變成一條偏微分方程｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
上一課得到兩個結果：作用量對時間的偏導數加上哈密頓量等於零，而作用量對每個座標的偏導數就是對應的動量。把哈密頓量裡的動量全部換成作用量對座標的偏導數，就得到一條只含作用量本身的一階偏微分方程，這就是漢彌頓－雅可比方程。它和拉格朗日方程、正則方程一樣，是一整套積分運動方程的方法的出發點。一階偏微分方程有個含任意函數的通解，但在力學裡我們要的不是它，而是完全積分：含有和獨立變數一樣多的獨立任意常數。獨立變數是時間和 s 個座標，所以完全積分要有 s 加一個常數；而作用量只以導數的形式出現，所以其中一個必定是相加的常數。關鍵的一步是把完全積分當成生成函數，把那 s 個任意常數當成新的動量，做一次正則變換。因為這個函數滿足漢彌頓－雅可比方程，新的哈密頓量正好等於零；哈密頓量為零，正則方程就說新的座標和新的動量全都是常數。於是把完全積分對每個常數求偏導數，令它等於另一個常數，就得到 s 條代數方程，把座標表示成時間和二倍 s 個常數的函數——這正是運動方程的通解，而動量再由作用量對座標的偏導數得到。系統保守時方程更簡單：時間只以減去能量乘時間的形式出現，代進去就得到只含座標的方程，也就是簡略作用量滿足的漢彌頓－雅可比方程。這條方程的幾何意義很漂亮：作用量的等值面就是波前，動量處處垂直於它們，質點的運動就像波前一層層往外傳，力學與光學在這裡真正合而為一。影片中段用兩個平面把整套方法的內容畫出來：左邊是普通的相平面，代表點沿著軌道不停地跑；右邊是新常數張成的平面，同一個運動在那裡是一個完全不動的點。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 47 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 47 | The Hamilton-Jacobi Equation: Mechanics in One Equation | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
The previous lesson gave two results: the derivative of the action with respect to time plus the Hamiltonian is zero, and the derivative of the action with respect to each coordinate is the corresponding momentum. Replacing every momentum in the Hamiltonian by the derivative of the action with respect to that coordinate gives a first-order partial differential equation containing only the action itself, and this is the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Like Lagrange's equations and the canonical equations, it is the starting point of a general method for integrating the equations of motion. A first-order partial differential equation has a general integral depending on an arbitrary function, but in mechanics what we want is a complete integral: one carrying as many independent arbitrary constants as there are independent variables. The independent variables are the time and the s coordinates, so a complete integral needs s plus one constants, and since the action enters only through its derivatives, one of them must be simply additive. Here is the key step: take the complete integral as a generating function and the s arbitrary constants as the new momenta, and carry out one canonical transformation. Because that function satisfies the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, the new Hamiltonian is exactly zero, and with a vanishing Hamiltonian the canonical equations say that all the new coordinates and momenta are constants. So differentiating the complete integral by each constant and setting the result equal to a new constant gives s algebraic equations, expressing the coordinates through the time and two s constants; that is the general integral of the equations of motion, and the momenta follow from the derivatives of the action. For a conservative system the equation is simpler: the time enters only as minus the energy times the time, and substituting leaves an equation in the coordinates alone, the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the abbreviated action. The geometry behind it is lovely: the level surfaces of the action are wavefronts, the momenta stand perpendicular to them everywhere, and the motion of the particle is the advance of those wavefronts, so that mechanics and optics genuinely become one subject. The middle of the video draws the whole content of the method with two planes: on the left the ordinary phase plane with the representative point running along its orbit, and on the right the plane of the new constants, where the very same motion is a point that does not move at all.

Lesson 47 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
